questions.question: The following pie-chart represents a total expenditure of Rs. 2,28,000 on different items in constructing a house in a town. What is the total expenditure done on Steel, Cement and Tiles?
questions.questionHtml:
The following pie-chart represents a total expenditure of Rs. 2,28,000 on different items in constructing a house in a town.

What is the total expenditure done on Steel, Cement and Tiles?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Total expenditure on different items is Rs2,28,000

CONCEPT USED:

100% represents total expenditure 

CALCULATION:

Here, 100% = Rs2,28,000

⇒ 1% =  Rs2280.

Now, expenditure done on steel, cement and tiles are 18%, 19% and 9% respectively.

Total expenditure = ( 18 + 19 + 9)% = 46%.

As 1% = 2280

⇒ 46% = 46 × 2280 = Rs104,880

Hence, total expenditure is Rs104,880.

Calculation:

On sports made by a country on various sports during 2019-2020

Quantity of the part = percentage × the total quantity of the whole.

questions.question: The following pie-chart shows the percentage-wise distribution of the number of students in five different schools P, Q, R, S and T. Total number of students in all five schools together is 8400. The number of students in school T is what percentage of the total number of students in schools Q and S together?
questions.questionHtml:
The following pie-chart shows the percentage-wise distribution of the number of students in five different schools P, Q, R, S and T. Total number of students in all five schools together is 8400.

The number of students in school T is what percentage of the total number of students in schools Q and S together?
questions.solution:
Given :

Pie chart showing the percentage-wise distribution

Percentage of the student in school T = 20%

Percentage of the student in school Q = 18%

Percentage of the student in school S = 22%

To find :

Percentage students of school T to school Q and S together

Concept used :

[(Student in school T)/(student in school Q + student in school S)] × 100

Calculation :

⇒ Students in school T = 20%

⇒ Students in school Q & S together = (18 + 20)%

⇒ Students in school Q & S together = 40%

⇒ Percentage students of school T to the school Q and S together = (20/40) × 100

⇒ Percentage students of school T to the school Q and S together = 50%

∴ The percentage of student of school T to school Q and S together is 50%.

Concept Used:

The concept of ratio is the comparison of two quantities of the same kind by division

Calculations:

⇒ Number of students who speak English = 15

⇒ Number of students who speak Bhojpuri = 10

⇒ Number of students who speak Tamil = 5

⇒ Total number of students who speak English and Bhojpuri = 15 + 10 = 25

⇒ The ratio of the Total number of students who speak English and Bhojpuri to the Number of students who speak Tamil = 25: 5 = 5: 1

Calculation:

Total sale of chocolate flavours = Rs. 5160

∴ The sale of vanilla is Rs. 3300.

questions.question: The pie-chart given below shows the monthly expenditures made by a family under different heads as percentages of the total monthly income of the family. If the total monthly income of the family is ₹70,000, then what is the amount that is left with the family after only the food and medical expenditures for the month are made?
questions.questionHtml: The pie-chart given below shows the monthly expenditures made by a family under different heads as percentages of the total monthly income of the family. If the total monthly income of the family is ₹70,000, then what is the amount that is left with the family after only the food and medical expenditures for the month are made?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total monthly income of a family = Rs 70,000

Percentage of expenditure for food = 28%

Percentage of expenditure for house rent = 14%

Percentage of expenditure for child education = 25%

Percentage of expenditure for medical = 10%

Percentage of expenditure for entertainment = 8%

Percentage of expenditure for provident fund = 15%

Concept Used:

Income left = Total Income – Income Spend

Calculation:

Amount spent on food = 28% of 70,000

Amount spent on food = \(\frac{28}{100}\) × 70000 = Rs 19,600

Amount spent on medical = 10% of 70,000

Amount spend on medical = \(\frac{10}{100}\) × 70000 = Rs 7,000

Total amount spent in food and medical = Rs 19,600 + Rs 7,000 = Rs 26,600

Amount left after spending on food and medical = Rs 70,000 – Rs 26,600 = Rs 43,400

∴ The amount left with the family after only the food and medical expenditures for the month is Rs 43,400

questions.question: The given pie chart shows the percentage distribution of 450 employees in an organisation. Study the pie chart and answer the question that follows. What is the central angel of the sector representing the number of employees in department A?
questions.questionHtml:

What is the central angel of the sector representing the number of employees in department A?
questions.solution:
Given:

Percentage of employees in department A

Formula used:

Central angle = 360° × (Percentage of employees in department A)/100%

Calculation:

Central angle = 360° × (Percentage of employees in department A)/100%

⇒ Central angle = 360° × 20%/100%

⇒ Central angle = 360°/5

⇒ Central angle = 72° 

∴ Central angel of the sector representing the number of employees in department A is 72°.

Shortcut Trick 

⇒ 100% = 360°

⇒ 1% = 360 / 100

∴ 20% = (360 / 100) × 20

⇒ 72°

questions.question: The pie-chart below illustrates the different fruit yields from a farmer's land that were sold to a fruit shop during a specific week. study the chart and answer the question that follows. If a total of 900 kg of fruits were sold that week, find the difference in sales (in kg) between oranges and grapes.
questions.questionHtml:
The pie-chart below illustrates the different fruit yields from a farmer's land that were sold to a fruit shop during a specific week. study the chart and answer the question that follows. 


If a total of 900 kg of fruits were sold that week, find the difference in sales (in kg) between oranges and grapes.
questions.solution:
Weight of oranges sold = 15% of 900 = 0.15 × 900 = 135 kg

Weight of grapes sold = 10% of 900 = 0.10 × 900 = 90 kg

Difference in sales between oranges and grapes = 135 - 90 = 45 kg

questions.question: The following pie chart shows the distribution of income from different taxes. Study the chart and answer the question. If the income from the market tax in a year is ₹260 crore, then the total income from other sources is : (in ₹ crore)
questions.questionHtml:
The following pie chart shows the distribution of income from different taxes. Study the chart and answer the question.

If the income from the market tax in a year is ₹260 crore, then the total income from other sources is : (in ₹ crore)
questions.solution:
Total income from all the sources = \(\frac{26}{100}\) × x = 260 ⇒ x = 260 × \(\frac{100}{26}\) = 1000

Income from other sources other than market tax = 1000 – 260 = 740

questions.question: Study the given pie-chart and answer the question that follows. The pie-chart shows the number of students (boys and girls) studying in standard 10 of various schools (X, Y, Z in the year 2022). What is the difference between the total number of students (boys and girls) in school Y and Z together and the total number of students (boys and girls) in school X and Y together?
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given pie-chart and answer the question that follows.

The pie-chart shows the number of students (boys and girls) studying in standard 10 of various schools (X, Y, Z in the year 2022). 


What is the difference between the total number of students (boys and girls) in school Y and Z together and the total number of students (boys and girls) in school X and Y together?
questions.solution:
Total number of students (boys and girls) in school Y and Z together = (30% + 25%) of 3600 ⇒ 55% of 3600 ⇒ 55/100 × 3600 = 1980

Total number of students (boys and girls) in school X and Y together = (45% + 30%) of 3600 ⇒  75% of 3600 ⇒  75/100 × 3600 = 2700

Required difference = 2700 - 1980 = 720

questions.question: The pie - chart shows percentage - wise distribution of teachers who teach six different subjects. Study the pie chart and answer the question: Total number of teachers = 1650 What is the total number of teachers teaching chemistry and biology?
questions.questionHtml:
The pie - chart shows percentage - wise distribution of teachers who teach six different subjects. Study the pie chart and answer the question:

Total number of teachers = 1650

What is the total number of teachers teaching chemistry and biology?
questions.solution:
From the pie chart, 

⇒ Number of teacher of chemistry = 24% of total number of teacher  

⇒ (24/100) × 1650 = 396 

⇒ NUmber of teacher of biology = 12% of total number of teacher 

⇒ (12/100) × 1650 = 198 

⇒ Total number of teacher teaching chemistry and biology = 396 + 198 = 594 

∴ the total number of teachers teaching chemistry and biology is 594

questions.question: Study the given pie-chart and answer the question that follows. The pie-chart shows the monthly expenditure incurred by a family on various items and their savings. If the total expenditure on education is Rs. 23,520, then what is the expenditure on clothing (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given pie-chart and answer the question that follows. 

The pie-chart shows the monthly expenditure incurred by a family on various items and their savings. 

If the total expenditure on education is Rs. 23,520, then what is the expenditure on clothing (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total expenditure on education = ₹23,520

Percentage spent on education = 28%

Percentage spent on clothing = 12%

Formula used:

Total Expenditure = (Expenditure on education / Percentage spent on education) × 100

Expenditure on clothing = (Percentage spent on clothing / 100) × Total Expenditure

Calculation:

Total Expenditure = (23,520 / 28) × 100 = 84,000

Expenditure on clothing = (12 / 100) × 84,000

⇒ Expenditure on clothing = 10,080

∴ The expenditure on clothing is ₹10,080.

questions.question: The given pie-chart represents the percentage of students enrolled in five different sports. The total number of students is 2800. What is the average number of students enrolled in Hockey and Tennis together ?
questions.questionHtml:
The given pie-chart represents the percentage of students enrolled in five different sports. The total number of students is 2800.

What is the average number of students enrolled in Hockey and Tennis together ?
questions.solution:
Given:

The number of students enrolled in hockey = 26% of 2800 

The number of students enrolled in Tennis = 14% of 2800 

Calculation:

The number of students enrolled in hockey = (26/100) × 2800 = 728 

The number of students enrolled in Tennis = (14/100) × 2800 = 392

Average number of students enrolled in Hockey and Tennis together = (728 + 392)/2 = 1120/2 

⇒ Average number of students enrolled = 560 

∴ The average number of students enrolled in Hockey and Tennis together is 560
